_comment: OPERATOR-OWED REGISTER — the durable record of work waiting on a human. Filed against BL-20260825-OPERATOR-OWED-ITEMS-HAVE-NO-REGISTER-NO-AGE-AND-NO-ESCALATION. Contract + why this shape: src/runtime/operator_owed.py (the pure grader) and docs/claude/operator-owed-register.md. Enforced by scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py, which FAILS CI when an item is carried across register commits without a state change. THIS IS NOT A BACKLOG: the backlogs hold DEFECTS; this holds items whose next action belongs to a person. Every item carries an owner_class, and 'unclassified' is refused. ⚠️ SERIALIZATION: this file is written with json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + a trailing newline. Re-dump it with EXACTLY those options — a different indent or ensure_ascii rewrites every line and buries a one-row change in a whole-file reformat (a 47,008-line diff for a 9-line change, reproduced twice in one day on the sibling backlog).

items.title: ib_paper MHG rests 200% stop cover across two disjoint OCA groups — cancel the leg that does NOT match trades.stop_loss
items.detail: STATE THE POPULATION: n=1 account/symbol, a single point-in-time read of /api/diag/ib_open_orders?account_id=ib_paper on 2026-08-25 — a 29-lot MHG position against two disjoint OCA groups (oca-protect-416, oca-protect-432), each carrying a 29-lot STP and a 29-lot LMT, so 58 of stop against 29 of position = 200%. Not a rate and not a distribution. OCA cancels only WITHIN a group, so one stop firing flattens the position and leaves the other group resting to sell 29 more into a naked SHORT.
items.severity_basis: ib_paper is a PAPER account, so this is not money-at-risk and is deliberately NOT graded critical — earlier hand-offs called it money-at-risk and that was inherited rather than checked. What keeps it high: the disjoint-OCA hazard is a naked-short shape, and the code path is the one real-money accounts use.
items.tier: 2 (a protective cancel on a live position)
items.owner_class_basis: The WIRE ALREADY EXISTS: cancel-ib-order and attach-ib-target are documented, allowlisted system-actions. This sat in the human column because ONE auto-remediation on 2026-08-20 cancelled the leg that MATCHED the journal (BL-20260820-OVERCOVER-REMEDIATION-CANCELLED-THE-JOURNAL-MATCHING-LEG). That distrusts the SELECTION, not the mechanism — and the repo already answered exactly this in src/runtime/protection_reassert.py by making the decision a pure function with non-collapsed states, so the policy is arguable in tests rather than against a live position. Re-classified from genuinely-human on 2026-08-25 by session 017etXEZ.
items.automation_path: scripts/ops/over_cover_proposal.py — reads /api/diag/ib_open_orders + the journal, runs the pure decision, and emits the exact cancel-ib-order system-action body. Dispatching it is Tier-2 and needs one operator OK.
items.next_action: NOT an operator dispatch — there is nothing to approve, because no repair path reaches this group. This item is BLOCKED ON WORK, not on a decision, and that work is BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL's residual: a cancel path that can reach a leg owned by the LIVE execution clientId without evicting the trader's session. Until that exists the honest state is 'detected, correctly refused, unreachable'. ⚠️ Do NOT let the absence of a path become a reason to reach for flatten-ib-position — that PLACES an order and is a different and larger action than clearing a stray protective leg. #10317 deliberately does NOT claim this is a generator: the keyed naming shipped recently and t4796 proves it is exercised, so 465 may simply pre-date it. Whether this is a finite backlog or ongoing is the first thing to MEASURE — count the legacy-named groups still resting and check whether any NEW one appeared after the keyed path deployed. That measurement, not a dispatch, is the next action.
items.carried_before_register_note: Self-reported from the three ✅ DONE board comments of 2026-08-25, recorded as the seed evidence only. The MEASURED carry count comes from this file's git history — see scripts/ci/check_operator_owed.py.
items.last_state_change_note: Withdrawn from the operator-owed register: the operator gave the direction (build the per-order cancel path) and the remaining work is engineering, tracked as BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL. The underlying over-cover is unrepaired and stays visible via OI-20260826-MHG-OVER-COVER-MECHANISM-UNVERIFIED.
items.resolution:
WITHDRAWN 2026-08-26 — it is not owed by the operator, and this row's own next_action already said so: 'NOT an operator dispatch — there is nothing to approve, because no repair path reaches this group. This item is BLOCKED ON WORK, not on a decision.' An item nobody can approve does not belong in a register of things awaiting approval; carrying it here made it a re-listing rather than an escalation, which is exactly what operator-owed-guard fired on (escalate_carried, 2 register commits).

WHAT THE OPERATOR ACTUALLY OWED WAS A DIRECTION, AND THEY GAVE IT (2026-08-26): build the per-order cancel path — a route that can cancel a leg owned by the LIVE execution clientId without evicting the trader's session. That decision is made, so nothing is outstanding on their side.

THE WORK IS OURS AND IS ALREADY TRACKED: BL-20260816-NO-PER-ORDER-IB-CANCEL (open) — 'No way to cancel a SINGLE IB order from any session; the only two mechanisms either PLACE another order or strip every protective stop on the account.' Related open rows: BL-20260826-A-LEGACY-NAMED-STRAY-GROUP-OWNED-BY-THE-TRADER-IS-UNREACHABLE-BY-BOTH-REPAIRS, BL-20260825-PLACE-PROTECTIVE-COUNTS-THE-CANCEL-CALL-NOT-ITS-EFFECT, BL-20260816-IB-CANCEL-ACCEPTED-BUT-NEVER-COMPLETES-VENUE-CLOSED.

⚠️ WITHDRAWN IS NOT FIXED. The 200% disjoint-OCA over-cover on ib_paper MHG is REAL and UNREPAIRED; ib_paper is a PAPER account so no money is at risk, and the DETECTION is working — a NEW over-cover paged the operator feed at 2026-08-26T15:17:19Z (ib_paper/MGC, 202%, 2 disjoint groups). What moved is only WHERE it is tracked. The live condition is carried by OI-20260826-MHG-OVER-COVER-MECHANISM-UNVERIFIED, which stays OPEN and loud.

items.title: DIAG_READ_TOKEN must be rotated — it was printed into TWO session transcripts on 2026-08-25
items.detail: Two sessions, one day, the same trap: `01X2zMCh` raised it and `018aKyS3` then reproduced the same ${VAR:-...} / ${VAR:+...} presence-test mistake and printed the token into a SECOND transcript. n=2 leaks. The correct presence test is [ -n "$VAR" ]. Note the repo is PUBLIC (since 2026-07-07), which is also why get-diag-token now refuses on a public repo (BL-20260818-GET-DIAG-TOKEN-EMITS-SECRET-TO-PUBLIC-SURFACE).
items.severity_basis: A live bearer for the whole /api/diag/* read surface, disclosed twice in one day. Every hour it is not rotated is an hour the disclosed value still authorizes.
items.tier: 2 (set-diag-token pushes the new value to the VM once the operator has minted it)
items.owner_class_basis: Only a person may MINT the new value and place it in the repo Actions secret — that is the one hand-off the autonomy mandate keeps with the operator, and on a PUBLIC repo get-diag-token deliberately refuses to hand a value back, so there is no session-side path to originate it.
items.automation_path: PARTIAL, and recorded so the human half is not overstated: once the operator has minted the value and set the Actions secret, the set-diag-token system-action pushes it to the VM and no human touches the VM. Only the origination is human.
items.next_action: Operator: mint a new DIAG_READ_TOKEN, set the repo Actions secret and the consuming environment's env var, then a session dispatches set-diag-token to the VM and verifies /api/diag/version answers on the new bearer and refuses the old one.

items.resolution: Closed on the operator's instruction, 2026-08-26: "it's done". ⚠️ RECORDED AS STATED, NOT AS VERIFIED — and the distinction is written here rather than smoothed over because a future session will read this row as the reason not to chase it. A session cannot read a secret's value, so no measurement of this was available to me either way; the basis is the operator's statement, which is the correct and sufficient basis for a secret_origination item, since originating and rotating the value is theirs alone to do.

items.title: breakout_1 needs a balance report (`bal <balance> <equity>`) — the prop cushion is unmeasured while the book is flat
items.detail: The prop bridge has no broker feed, so the account-status snapshot is only ever as fresh as the operator's last report. Measured 2026-08-25: the latest snapshot was 47.4h old against a PROP_STATUS_REQUEST_MAX_AGE_HOURS threshold of 24h. The static DD floor is an ACCOUNT-level line that binds while flat, and flat is exactly when the next ticket is sized against a cushion nobody has measured.
items.severity_basis: It is an input to prop_balance's sizing-freshness gate AND the /api/bot/prop/status rule-distance panel. A stale cushion renders identically to a live one to any consumer that reads only `present`.
items.tier: 1 (the bot already asks; the answer is the operator's)
items.owner_class_basis: The number exists only on the Breakout terminal, for which this repo holds no API — the manual bridge IS the integration. A person must read the terminal and report it; no wire could exist without a broker API we do not have.
items.cannot_automate_reason: No broker API exists for Breakout — the prop integration is a documented manual bridge by design (Telegram ticket out, operator report back). The bot's half is already automated: prop_status_request asks on its own cadence and prop_fills_staleness alerts when a moved balance goes unreported. There is nothing left on our side to build.
items.next_action: Operator: send `bal <balance> <equity>` to the prop bot, or a terminal screenshot (screenshot_parse reads it). Either lands through the one prop_report.ingest_report chokepoint.
items.carried_before_register_note: Self-reported seed; the measured carry comes from git history.
items.last_state_change_note: Operator reported the terminal state; journalled through prop_report.ingest_report.
items.resolution: ACTED, not re-listed. The operator sent Breakout terminal screenshots 2026-08-28; the state was journalled through the one prop_report.ingest_report chokepoint as three reports: SOLUSDT close (exit 103.07, +78.25, fill id 38), ETHUSDT close (exit 2480.00, -77.22, fill id 39), and an account_status of balance/equity 4757.93 flat. Both closes reconcile EXACTLY against the already-journalled entries: (103.07-99.94)*25.0=+78.25 and (2480.00-2531.48)*1.5=-77.22. /api/bot/prop/status now reads freshness 'ok' (was 'stale' at 31.1h). WHAT THE ANSWER CHANGED, and it is not the reassuring direction: the book is FLAT and the static-DD cushion is $57.93 (4757.93 - 4700.00), NOT the $176 the 08-27 snapshot implied and NOT the $64 this row recorded from 08-25. The ETHUSDT position closed at 2480.00 against a declared stop of 2480.71535714 -- a stop-out. distance_to_daily_loss_usd remains None (day_pnl_state 'realized_unreported'), so the daily-loss cushion is still unmeasured even now. Two defects were found BY DOING THIS and are filed separately: BL-20260828-PROP-REPORT-CONCURRENCY-SILENTLY-CANCELS-A-QUEUED-REPORT and BL-20260828-RULE-DISTANCE-DOUBLE-COUNTS-A-LATE-REPORTED-EARLIER-FILL.
items.escalated_2026_08_26: STILL OPEN AND NOW MATERIAL, not merely stale. On 2026-08-26T22:18Z the operator opened a prop position against this unmeasured cushion: breakout_1 SOLUSD long 25.00 @ 99.94 (fill id 36, ticket prop-manual-784e35819c9f). At the ticket's declared stop 96.33535714 that position risks (99.94 - 96.33535714) * 25 = $90.12. The ONLY account-status snapshot in the journal -- balance 4764.00, reported 2026-08-23T16:10:45Z, 78.2h old, freshness 'stale' -- leaves $64.00 to the static drawdown floor of $4,700. On those figures a full stop-out BREACHES the floor by about $26 and permanently disables the account. STATE THE POPULATION: that $64.00 is derived from ONE snapshot, three days old; the balance can only have moved since, and the emitted ticket carried this same CUSHION UNKNOWN warning in its own text. This is why the row is owed.

items.title: Decide alpaca_live's `daily_usd: 200` — the measured paper drawdowns say it would trip routinely
items.detail:
alpaca_live's risk block is exactly {max_dd_pct: 0.1, daily_loss_pct: 0.1, daily_usd: 200, risk_pct: 0.05} (⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-26 by reading config/accounts.yaml: this row previously stated 0.05/0.05/0.02 and was stale on EVERY value — field beats comment, and this row is what a future session reads to make this exact decision) — no max_gross_exposure_pct, no max_position_pct, no notional cap. Against it, the paper-portfolio mirror's maxDrawdown is -14,995 (51 trades, window=all, pnlCoverage 0.549) and all-paper is -115,509 (574 trades, pnlCoverage 0.348), versus a proposed real-money funding of roughly $2,500-$25,000. ⚠️ Read the coverage before the PnL: a third to a half of it is measured.

=== 2026-08-26 — OPERATOR DECISION: LEAVE daily_usd AT 200. ===
Funding level given by the operator: **$200**. At that equity `daily_usd: 200` is INERT — it equals 100% of the account, while `daily_loss_pct: 0.1` binds first at $20. It only begins to bind above **$2,000** equity (200 / 0.10), so it is a dormant backstop that arms itself automatically if the account is ever funded past that. Operator chose to leave it; no config change was made.
⚠️ **The account is `mode: dry_run`**, which is the actual explanation for the zero gross notional across 91 exposure_soak rows cited in this row's own severity_basis — the execution gate, not a sizing failure, and consistent with BL-20260824-SILENT-REFUSAL-CANNOT-SEE-A-DECLARED-DRY-RUN. Any future reading of 'flat' on this account must establish the mode first.
⚠️ **A SIZING FLOOR EXISTS AT THIS FUNDING and is a precondition of the funding decision, not a consequence of it** — see BL-20260826-ALPACA-LIVE-AT-200-USD-CANNOT-SIZE-ITS-LARGEST-SYMBOLS.
items.severity_basis: alpaca_live is not funded, so nothing is at risk today — this gates a FUTURE funding decision rather than describing a live exposure. It is not low because the decision is a precondition of that funding.
items.owner_class_basis: Setting a risk cap is Tier-3 by the permission tiers — the value expresses how much the operator is willing to lose in a day, which is a preference, not a lookup. A session may analyse and propose the exact change; it may not take it.
items.next_action: Operator decision on the value, with the two measured populations above in front of them. A session can prepare the exact diff and the funding-level arithmetic; the number is the operator's.
items.carried_before_register_note: Self-reported seed; the measured carry comes from git history.
items.last_state_change_note: Operator set funding at $200 and chose to LEAVE daily_usd at 200 (inert below $2,000 equity; no config change). The stale risk block in this row was corrected against config/accounts.yaml. Row stays OPEN: the cap decision is settled at the CURRENT funding only, and the sizing floor filed alongside is unresolved.
items.resolution: ANSWERED by the operator 2026-08-26 and shipped as record in #10347: funding is $200 and daily_usd STAYS at 200. Recorded honestly as a decision with a consequence rather than as a tidy close: at $200 funding, daily_usd: 200 is INERT -- it equals 100% of the account while daily_loss_pct: 0.1 binds first at $20 -- and it arms itself only above $2,000 equity (200 / 0.10). Left in place as a dormant backstop, per the operator. config/accounts.yaml and config/strategies.yaml were NOT touched. The sizing consequence of the same funding level is filed separately and is NOT closed by this decision: BL-20260826-ALPACA-LIVE-AT-200-USD-CANNOT-SIZE-ITS-LARGEST-SYMBOLS (population: the 10 of 11 declared symbols for which /api/bot/candles returned a close on 2026-08-26; at a 5% stop 4 of 10 round to ZERO shares). Inert while the account is mode: dry_run; it binds the moment it goes live at this funding.

items.title: Delete the stray branch claude/ib-breaker-peer-close — nothing in it is unmerged
items.detail: Session `qhpxyh` pushed one commit to it before remembering its session was pinned to another branch, then could not delete it: `git push --delete` failed with a transport disconnect, and it was handed to a human on that basis.
items.severity_basis: Repo hygiene. Nothing depends on it and nothing is lost while it stands.
items.owner_class_basis: It reached the human column because a push failed in one session — and MEASURED here 2026-08-25, the failure is real but is not a permission boundary for the SYSTEM: `git push origin --delete` returns HTTP 403 on four attempts with backoff from a session's credential, while a normal push from that same credential in the same minute succeeds. Deleting a branch needs no human judgement, no minted secret and no broker — a runner's own GITHUB_TOKEN can do it. Nobody had built the wire, which is the definition of defaulted_to_human. Recording it as 'cannot be automated' would have been this register's own anti-pattern, one size down.
items.automation_path: .github/workflows/prune-merged-claude-branch.yml — issue-triggered (label `prune-merged-branch`) or workflow_dispatch. Dry-run by default; `claude/**` only; prints the unmerged-commit list and refuses unless it is empty or `force: true` carries a reason.
items.next_action: Dispatch it with `branch: claude/ib-breaker-peer-close`, `apply: true`, `force: true` and the reason below. ⚠️ The workflow must be on the DEFAULT branch before an issue trigger or a dispatch can reach it, so this fires after the PR merges — not a hand-off, a sequencing fact.
items.carried_before_register_note: Self-reported seed; the measured carry comes from git history.
items.last_state_change_note: Resolved. THE FIRST ITEM TO TRAVEL THE WHOLE REGISTER: seeded as a human hand-off, re-classified defaulted_to_human on measured evidence (HTTP 403 from a session credential, which is a boundary for that credential and not for a runner), the missing wire built, then dispatched and confirmed. Nobody was asked to do anything.
items.resolution: DELETED via .github/workflows/prune-merged-claude-branch.yml, run 32899747507 (workflow_dispatch, apply:true force:true). The dry run (32899662020) REFUSED first and printed its evidence: one commit 89ceea0b not an ancestor of main, and git cherry '-' meaning a patch-equivalent IS on main. That refusal is the guard working, not an obstacle: squash-merge is why the branch is not an ancestor, which is exactly the case the reasoned waiver exists for. Before forcing, both rows the branch adds were re-verified byte-identical on main by field-by-field JSON comparison IN THIS SESSION (not taken from the earlier note), with zero branch rows absent from main. Deletion confirmed independently afterwards: git ls-remote --heads for the ref returns nothing. The waiver reason is recorded in the run log.
